title: Infinitely many knot types in the symmetric ABC flow
credit: Etnyre & Ghrist (2000), arXiv:math-ph/9906021; Enciso, Peralta-Salas (and Romaniega), arXiv:2006.15033.
premise_risks: arXiv:2609.17449 (Szumiński–Llibre, 2026 preprint): cited only as related perturbative work; nothing in the statement depends on it.
plain: Steady Euler flows can carry knotted streamlines, and generic high-frequency Beltrami fields on the torus contain every knot. Show that the most-studied explicit example, the ABC flow with A = B = C = 1, has closed streamlines tied in infinitely many different knots.
math: Let $X=(\sin z+\cos y,\ \sin x+\cos z,\ \sin y+\cos x)$ on $\mathbb T^3=(\mathbb R/2\pi\mathbb Z)^3$ (a curl eigenfield, $\nabla\times X=X$). Prove that the periodic orbits of $X$ that lie in some embedded 3-ball $B\subset\mathbb T^3$ realize infinitely many distinct knot types (as knots in $B\cong$ a ball in $\mathbb R^3$). Stronger: every knot type is realized.
